question: Which vaccine is routinely given to newborns to protect against severe forms of childhood TB?

options.A: OPV vaccine
options.B: BCG vaccine
options.C: MMR vaccine
options.D: Tetanus toxoid

explanation: The BCG vaccine is given early in life to give babies strong backup against the most dangerous, widespread forms of childhood TB.

question: Which major organ system is most immediately threatened by severe hyperkalemia (high blood potassium)?

options.A: Skeletal muscle system
options.B: Gastrointestinal tract
options.C: Cardiovascular system
options.D: Integumentary system

explanation: High potassium levels dangerously alter the electrical conduction of the heart, leading to fatal arrhythmias. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T2#GNS315_U2_T2_h7)

question: What makes farming pesticides particularly dangerous in rural areas?

options.A: Farmers use them exclusively as food flavoring agents in local dishes
options.B: They are frequently stored near food items and handled without protective gear
options.C: They only affect animals and have zero toxic impact on human physiology
options.D: They lose their toxicity completely within a few minutes of application

explanation: Spot on! When chemicals are kept close to food and used without gloves or masks, accidental poisoning happens easily.

question: What is a defining feature of Community-Based Health Insurance (CBHI) schemes?

options.A: They are funded exclusively through international oil company taxes
options.B: They are mandatory for all federal government civil servants
options.C: They provide free specialized surgeries in foreign teaching hospitals
options.D: They are nonprofit prepaid pools managed locally by community members

explanation: CBHI schemes rely on small, regular contributions managed right at the grassroots level to cover local health needs. Community power in action!

question: Why do many terminal patients and their families choose home-based palliative care?

options.A: It guarantees that the terminal illness will suddenly go into full remission
options.B: It allows the patient to spend time in a familiar environment with loved ones
options.C: It is completely free with zero financial planning required
options.D: It removes the need for any nursing involvement whatsoever

explanation: Being at home offers comfort and surrounds the patient with familiar people and belongings during end-of-life stages. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T8#GNS324_U1_T8_h5)

question: What are you trying to find out when you perform Leopold's maneuvers on a pregnant client?

options.A: To check the mother's cardiovascular health status
options.B: To stimulate the uterus into early contraction
options.C: To determine fetal lie, presentation, and engagement
options.D: To measure the exact weight of the placenta

explanation: Leopold's maneuvers are just feeling the bump with your hands to figure out how the baby is curled up and positioned inside as delivery gets closer.

question: Why is a baby with neonatal tetanus at high risk for aspiration pneumonia?

options.A: Swallowing difficulties and tube feeding increase risk
options.B: High fever melts the protective airway mucus
options.C: The bacterial toxin directly attacks lung tissue
options.D: The lungs produce excessive fluid naturally

explanation: Spot on! Because they cannot swallow normally and rely on tube feeding, it is much easier for fluids or milk to accidentally enter the lungs.

question: Which of these is NOT a common cause of neurasthenia?

options.A: Overwhelming family responsibilities
options.B: Eating a high-protein diet
options.C: Severe occupational strain
options.D: Chronic financial hardship

explanation: Nice one! Eating healthy food doesn't cause nervous exhaustion. Money worries, work stress, and family pressures are the real triggers here.

question: What is a likely consequence of poor communication among home health team members?

options.A: Conflicting instructions given to the patient and family
options.B: Reduced need for interprofessional documentation
options.C: Better alignment between nursing and therapy goals
options.D: Faster recovery times due to independent decision-making

explanation: When team members fail to communicate, patients and caregivers may receive mixed guidance, leading to confusion and safety risks. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T4#GNS324_U1_T4_h6)

question: What do we call the large amount of urine passed in the first few days after having a baby?

options.A: Tubular necrosis
options.B: Glomerular shutdown
options.C: Postpartum diuresis
options.D: Renal exhaustion

explanation: Postpartum diuresis is just the body's way of getting rid of all that extra pregnancy fluid it doesn't need anymore. Frequent trips to the bathroom are expected!

question: What is improvement fatigue in a clinical setting?

options.A: Exhaustion caused by lifting heavy patients without mechanical assistance
options.B: Feeling overwhelmed by an endless stream of new mandates and quality targets
options.C: Physical tiredness caused by walking too many miles during a night shift
options.D: A rare muscle disease that affects nurses working in intensive care

explanation: Too many overlapping projects exhaust staff mental energy, causing them to resist any further operational changes. [learn more](GST319_U1_T5#GST319_U1_T5_h6)

question: Which situation can instantly plunge a family into a deep emotional crisis?

options.A: Attending a community health talk
options.B: Going for a routine yearly check-up at the clinic
options.C: Learning how to take home medications properly
options.D: A main breadwinner getting hit with a serious, long-term illness

explanation: When unexpected illness strikes the person providing for the home, it shatters family stability and money security all at once.

question: Which of these is an example of a non-clinical outsourced hospital service?

options.A: Administering intravenous medications
options.B: Hospital laundry and facility maintenance
options.C: Specialized renal dialysis procedures
options.D: Diagnostic laboratory blood testing

explanation: Things like cleaning, washing linens, and security are support services that don't involve direct medical treatment, making them great for outsourcing.

question: Why must the tools used to collect data in explanatory research be valid and reliable?

options.A: To prevent the hospital from paying research fees
options.B: To ensure the measurements are accurate and trustworthy
options.C: To reduce the total number of participants required
options.D: To make sure the questionnaires are printed in full color

explanation: Awesome! Reliable tools mean your measurements can be trusted and will give consistent results every time.

question: What is the simplest way to describe what a drug does in the body?

options.A: Any synthetic material used strictly for laboratory testing
options.B: A compound that creates entirely new cellular functions in organs
options.C: Any chemical substance that alters biological function in a living body
options.D: A natural substance derived exclusively from plants for nourishment

explanation: Spot on! Drugs work by modifying what your body is already doing—they don't magically invent brand-new functions. You've got this!

question: Why is it important for a patient to empty her bladder right before an MVA procedure?

options.A: To stop the kidneys from producing urine for the next several hours
options.B: To prevent accidental urine contamination of the surgical field
options.C: To test kidney function before giving any local anesthetic drugs
options.D: To make the pelvic exam and uterine positioning easier and less painful

explanation: A full bladder displaces the uterus, makes bimanual palpation difficult, and increases patient discomfort during speculum and instrument insertion. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h4)

question: What key physical features must a proper sharps container have?

options.A: Transparent and open at the top
options.B: Biodegradable and water-soluble
options.C: Puncture-resistant and leak-proof
options.D: Made of soft, flexible cardboard

explanation: Sharps bins have to be tough! Being puncture-resistant and leak-proof ensures that needles won't poke through and fluids won't spill out while waiting for disposal.

question: How can you, as a nurse, directly help manage resources well in a health facility?

options.A: By avoiding waste and using medical supplies properly
options.B: By increasing the price of medications for patients
options.C: By handling all financial accounting tasks
options.D: By refusing to treat uninsured individuals

explanation: Every bandage and syringe counts! Being careful with supplies helps stretch limited healthcare funds so more patients can get help.

question: Which of the following is NOT a common complication of chronic hypochondriasis?

options.A: Financial stress from excessive medical appointments
options.B: Risks from unnecessary invasive medical procedures
options.C: Strain on marital and family relationships
options.D: Permanent physical immunity to all infectious diseases

explanation: You got it! Illness anxiety definitely doesn't give you superpower immunity; instead, it brings relationship strain, money troubles, and risks from needless procedures.

question: Which part of the brain acts as the master control center to start the menstrual cycle?

options.A: The adrenal gland
options.B: The thyroid gland
options.C: The pituitary gland
options.D: The hypothalamus

explanation: Think of the hypothalamus as the head office in the brain—it sends the very first signal (GnRH) to kick off the cycle!

question: A diabetic patient insists on participating in a religious fast that could affect their blood sugar. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Discharge the patient immediately for being uncooperative
options.B: Tell the patient that religion has no place in modern healthcare
options.C: Collaborate with the patient to find safe ways to manage blood sugar during the fast
options.D: Force the patient to eat hospital meals against their religious beliefs

explanation: Respecting patient autonomy and beliefs while finding safe health compromises is the core of ethical nursing care. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T001#GNS227_U7_T001_h6)

question: Which principle of intersectoral collaboration focuses on putting the most vulnerable people first?

options.A: Specialization
options.B: Privatization
options.C: Equity
options.D: Centralization

explanation: You've got it! Equity means fairness—making sure resources and care reach the people who need them the most, rather than just splitting everything equally.

question: Which mineral deficiency is particularly common in mountainous regions and areas far from the sea?

options.A: Calcium
options.B: Sodium
options.C: Vitamin C
options.D: Iodine

explanation: Iodine is naturally abundant in oceans and coastal soils, leaving inland and high-altitude regions vulnerable to low dietary intake. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T022#GNS227_U2_T022_h3)

question: What is a major plus of using the intraperitoneal route instead of pills for belly issues?

options.A: It completely avoids the need for any sterile equipment or supplies
options.B: It allows patients to self-administer complex chemotherapy at home
options.C: It delivers higher local drug concentrations directly to the target area
options.D: It eliminates all risks of systemic side effects and infection

explanation: Brilliant! Going straight to the source means the medication hits the problem area hard and fast, way better than waiting for a pill to digest. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T11#GNS125_U3_T11_h7)

question: What is the leading cause of severe trauma and head injuries on our roads here in Nigeria?

options.A: Road traffic accidents
options.B: Severe seasonal flooding
options.C: Industrial chemical spills
options.D: Household gas explosions

explanation: Sadly, road traffic accidents are the top reason emergency wards see severe injuries. Stay safe out there!

question: Why is a first-come, first-served system a bad idea in emergency room triage?

options.A: It takes too much time for computer systems to log patients in order
options.B: Patients prefer waiting longer periods for their evaluations
options.C: Hospital administrators legally forbid using arrival times for care
options.D: It could cause a critically ill patient to die in the waiting room while a minor case is seen first

explanation: Triage ensures that limited life-saving resources go straight to the sickest patients first, preventing tragic delays.

question: Poor mouth care in vulnerable patients is closely linked to which serious lung problem?

options.A: Aspiration pneumonia
options.B: Spontaneous pneumothorax
options.C: Pulmonary embolism
options.D: Obstructive sleep apnea

explanation: Spot on! Germs hiding in a dirty mouth can slip down into the lungs and cause a nasty infection called aspiration pneumonia.

question: What tool do healthcare teams commonly use to help cut down on harmful clinical variation?

options.A: Randomized staff schedule changes every morning
options.B: Eliminating all shift handover meetings entirely
options.C: Punitive disciplinary letters for minor charting delays
options.D: Standardized checklists and clinical pathways

explanation: Brilliant! Checklists make our steps clear so that care stays consistent no matter which shift is on duty.

question: What is an 'outlier' on a scatter diagram?

options.A: A data point located far away from the main pattern
options.B: The average score calculated for the entire group
options.C: The very first dot plotted on the bottom left corner
options.D: A label written incorrectly on the vertical axis

explanation: An outlier is just a rebel dot that sits far away from everyone else's general trend. You'll spot them easily!

question: How can you make sure your patient truly understands a new reproductive medication?

options.A: By assuming the pharmacist already covered everything needed
options.B: By handing the patient a technical textbook to read alone
options.C: By focusing only on how much the prescription costs
options.D: By explaining expected benefits, side effects, and warning signs clearly

explanation: Exactly! Taking time to explain how the drug works and what side effects to watch for helps your patient stay safe and confident.

question: Why do home health nurses need to watch out for non-physical abuse just as much?

options.A: Emotional abuse always leaves visible marks on medical charts
options.B: Physical abuse never occurs without emotional coercion first
options.C: Coercion, control, and isolation are core dynamics of domestic abuse
options.D: Non-physical abuse is the only type reportable by law

explanation: You've got this! Abuse isn't only physical. Emotional and psychological control can trap and break a person just as deeply as physical blows.

question: What does 'loss to follow-up' mean in the context of a longitudinal prospective study?

options.A: Nurses forget to check the patient's vital signs during a routine shift
options.B: Participants drop out, move away, or stop responding before the research is completed
options.C: Researchers accidentally delete all computer files from the first day of the study
options.D: The hospital misplaces the budget allocated for patient transportation

explanation: Attrition threatens study validity when participants who leave differ systematically from those who stay until the final evaluation. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T15#GNS224_U1_T15_h4)

question: In public health, what do we mean by an epidemiological 'agent'?

options.A: The primary factor that must be present for a disease to occur
options.B: The vector that carries a microbe from place to place
options.C: The immune response produced by a healthy host
options.D: The physical environment where a patient lives

explanation: Think of the agent as the root cause or spark—like a bacterium or virus—without which the disease simply cannot happen. You've got this!

question: Which of these questions shows great communication during a diet check-in?

options.A: Are you aware that eating junk food causes heart disease?
options.B: What types of snacks do you usually eat in the evening?
options.C: Why have you not followed the low-fat diet I gave you?
options.D: Do you eat too much sugar every single day?

explanation: You got it! Open-ended questions make patients feel comfortable talking openly without feeling judged or cornered.

question: Which situation means a child needs intravenous (IV) fluids right away?

options.A: Low-grade fever lasting less than an hour
options.B: A slight decrease in daily appetite
options.C: Mild loose stool passed twice in one day
options.D: Severe dehydration with signs of shock

explanation: When shock and severe dehydration set in, drinking isn't enough anymore. IV fluids are urgently needed to restore blood pressure and save the day.

question: What is an essential first step for a nurse providing effective sexual health advocacy?

options.A: Overcoming personal discomfort and professional biases
options.B: Referring every patient directly to a psychiatric hospital
options.C: Writing research papers on rare reproductive diseases
options.D: Requiring patients to sign a formal intimacy contract

explanation: Nurses must first address their own biases and discomfort to create a safe, welcoming environment for their patients. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T26#GNS312_U1_T26_h8)

question: Which of these is a standard metric used to check the quality of home health care?

options.A: The brand of uniforms worn by the nursing staff
options.B: Frequency of internal staff birthday parties
options.C: Total number of parking spaces at the agency office
options.D: Rates of unplanned hospital readmissions

explanation: Tracking readmission rates tells us a lot: if patients keep returning to the hospital, it might mean home care plans need tweaking to keep them stable.

question: What is the function of the flexible plastic canulas used in an MVA kit?

options.A: To seal the outside opening of the vagina during suction
options.B: To travel through the cervix and vacuum out uterine tissue
options.C: To measure the exact internal temperature of the uterus
options.D: To pump local anesthetic pain medicine into the cervix

explanation: Canulas are the sterile tubes inserted past the cervix into the uterus to channel the suctioned tissue into the syringe. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h3)

question: What happens when you take in more food energy (calories) than your body burns off?

options.A: Excess energy is stored primarily as fat
options.B: The body uses up its protein stores completely
options.C: Cellular chemical reactions stop entirely
options.D: Metabolic rate drops permanently to zero

explanation: Think of it like money: if you earn more than you spend, you save the extra! The body packs away extra calories as fat tissue to use for a rainy day.

question: What is the fastest, most effective way to stop severe bleeding on a patient's arm or leg?

options.A: Give them water to drink to replace lost blood
options.B: Lift the legs up high
options.C: Apply direct pressure or a tourniquet
options.D: Apply ice packs directly to the wound

explanation: Well done! Direct pressure or a tourniquet squeezes those bleeding vessels shut and stops dangerous blood loss fast.

question: What is the link between physical disability and poverty in developing regions like Nigeria?

options.A: They share a cycle where each makes the other worse
options.B: Poverty completely protects people from impairments
options.C: Disability guarantees instant wealth
options.D: They have no connection at all

explanation: Poverty can lead to accidents and lack of healthcare (causing disability), and living with a disability can make earning an income harder. It's a tough cycle!

question: How often should a bedbound patient be turned to help prevent pressure injuries?

options.A: Only when requested
options.B: Every two hours
options.C: Once every shift
options.D: Every four hours

explanation: Turning a bedbound patient at least every two hours relieves pressure on bony prominences and restores blood flow to vulnerable tissues. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T9#GNS225_U5_T9_h4)

question: Which instrument is best for capturing deep, personal stories from patients about chronic illness?

options.A: Interview guide
options.B: Simple questionnaire
options.C: Blood pressure cuff
options.D: Checklist of bedside actions

explanation: Interview guides allow researchers to ask open-ended questions and explore personal experiences in detail. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T21#GNS224_U1_T21_h3)

question: What exactly is a 'maternal near miss'?

options.A: A baby delivered prematurely who required care in the special care baby unit
options.B: A woman who experiences mild morning sickness throughout her pregnancy
options.C: A woman who nearly died from a pregnancy complication but survived
options.D: A pregnant woman who almost missed her scheduled antenatal care clinic

explanation: A near-miss is when a mother faces a life-threatening crisis but thankfully pulls through, thanks to quick medical help or pure luck.

question: What is a major risk associated with using unregulated herbal mixtures?

options.A: Lowered financial costs for the family
options.B: Immediate cure of all psychiatric disorders
options.C: Permanent immunity to infectious diseases
options.D: Organ toxicity from incorrect dosing

explanation: True dat! Without standardized measurements or quality control, traditional herbal mixtures can sometimes cause accidental poisoning and organ damage.

question: What is the main goal of targeted temperature management after a patient is successfully revived?

options.A: To prevent the development of blood clots in the legs
options.B: To protect the brain from injury caused by lack of oxygen
options.C: To lower the heart rate back down to normal resting levels
options.D: To stop the patient from shivering and burning calories

explanation: Cooling the body down slows down brain activity, giving injured brain cells a much better chance to recover after a cardiac arrest.

question: A patient with severe malaria hesitates to see a doctor because they have no cash. What reform fixes this?

options.A: A policy requiring cash deposits before any nursing assessment
options.B: Increasing taxes on everyday food and household items
options.C: Closing public clinics to save money on utility bills
options.D: Subsidized health insurance schemes that cover treatment costs

explanation: Health insurance steps in so patients can get treated for illnesses like malaria without needing cash right at the hospital door.

question: How does pulmonary circulation differ from systemic circulation?

options.A: Pulmonary circulation bypasses the right side of the heart
options.B: Pulmonary circulation operates under much lower pressure
options.C: Systemic circulation only carries deoxygenated blood
options.D: Systemic circulation has a shorter pathway than pulmonary

explanation: The pulmonary circuit is a low-pressure pathway because the lungs are close to the heart and offer less resistance than the entire systemic body. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T9#GNS111_U2_T9_h1)

question: What does it mean for a research problem to be measurable?

options.A: The results can be guessed without collecting any data
options.B: Every patient in the hospital must agree with the findings
options.C: Its concepts can be clearly quantified using valid tools or scales
options.D: It can be measured using a simple household ruler

explanation: A measurable problem means you can use clear tools, scores, or observations to track and analyze your study variables accurately.

question: Which hormone relaxes the muscles of the urinary tract during pregnancy, causing the ureters to widen?

options.A: Progesterone
options.B: Prolactin
options.C: Estrogen
options.D: Oxytocin

explanation: Progesterone relaxes smooth muscles all over the body. During pregnancy, this causes the tubes carrying urine from the kidneys to widen. You've got this!

question: A nurse wants to chat with a patient across a state border using a regular social media app. What is the main risk here?

options.A: The phone battery will drain too quickly during the chat
options.B: Potential breach of privacy and possible licensing violations
options.C: The patient will refuse to take their prescribed medication
options.D: Social media apps always improve the accuracy of vital signs

explanation: Careful! Public social media apps aren't secure for health data, and practicing across regions without proper clearance can break professional rules.

question: Which tiny blood vessels are mainly responsible for leaking fluid into the tissues when oedema starts?

options.A: Large veins
options.B: Arteriole valves
options.C: Capillaries
options.D: Lymphatic ducts

explanation: You've got it! Capillaries are the microscopic vessels where fluid normally slips back and forth between blood and tissue. When things go wrong, they leak extra fluid.

question: What is the primary purpose of human nutrition for body cells?

options.A: Increasing core body temperature overnight
options.B: Eliminating toxins through the renal system
options.C: Providing chemical substances for survival and repair
options.D: Regulating the speed of electrical nerve impulses

explanation: Nutrition supplies the raw chemical materials that cells need to stay alive, grow, and repair themselves daily. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T015#GNS227_U2_T015_h1)

question: Why do we say out-of-pocket spending is a rough deal for patients?

options.A: It forces families to pay directly at the point of care, leading to financial hardship
options.B: It requires too much paperwork for hospital administrators
options.C: It completely eliminates the need for government hospitals
options.D: It increases the overall supply of essential medicines too quickly

explanation: Paying cash right at the hospital door can wipe out a family's savings overnight when a sudden sickness hits. That's why health insurance is so important!

question: A researcher wants to study how nurses feel about working night shifts by having open conversations. Which data collection method is best?

options.A: Numerical blood pressure screening
options.B: In-depth qualitative interviews
options.C: A rigid multiple-choice questionnaire
options.D: Laboratory biomarker blood testing

explanation: Open-ended interviews are fantastic because they let nurses express their true feelings in their own words.

question: A mum receiving magnesium sulfate has a breathing rate of 8 breaths per minute and her knee reflexes are gone. What is your very first action?

options.A: Write it down as normal and keep watching.
options.B: Turn up the drip because the dose is too small.
options.C: Tell her to drink plenty of water.
options.D: Stop the magnesium infusion right away and tell the doctor.

explanation: Slow breathing and missing reflexes mean too much magnesium is building up in her body (toxicity)! Stop the infusion immediately and get help—calcium gluconate is the antidote.

question: What is a common belief among patients that drives the overuse of injections in many communities?

options.A: Oral medications have no side effects at all
options.B: Syringes contain vitamins that protect against malaria
options.C: Injections are more potent and work faster than oral drugs
options.D: Pills are more expensive than intravenous infusions

explanation: Many patients genuinely believe that if medicine isn't injected into their skin or veins, it's just 'too weak' to cure them. Patient education is our superpower here!

question: What are the three simple action steps in Psychological First Aid (PFA)?

options.A: Assess, Diagnose, and Treat
options.B: Observe, Intervene, and Evaluate
options.C: Search, Rescue, and Stabilize
options.D: Look, Listen, and Link

explanation: Easy to remember: Look for safety, Listen with empathy, and Link people to the help they need. You've got this!

question: What is a basic rule of good manners when arriving at a patient's home?

options.A: Knock, greet household members politely, and ask permission to enter
options.B: Begin treatment immediately without washing hands
options.C: Walk right in without knocking to save time
options.D: Park your car directly in the neighbor's driveway

explanation: You got it! It's their private property, so simple courtesy like knocking and greeting everyone sets a warm and professional tone.

question: Which simple tool do nurses commonly use to screen adult patients for distant vision problems?

options.A: Otoscope
options.B: Snellen chart
options.C: Ophthalmoscope
options.D: Tuning fork

explanation: The Snellen chart is the classic eye chart with rows of letters that we use to check how clearly someone can see from a distance. Great clinical tool to keep in mind!

question: How should you properly correct a mistake in a paper family planning register?

options.A: Scratch out the word multiple times until it is unreadable
options.B: Apply thick correction fluid over the mistake until it disappears
options.C: Draw a single line through the error, write the correction, and initial it
options.D: Tear out the entire page and rewrite the whole register

explanation: A single strike-through is standard nursing practice because it keeps the original entry visible while showing the correction clearly, alongside your initials.

question: Which body receptor is mainly responsible for the pain-relieving power of strong opioids?

options.A: Alpha receptor
options.B: Mu receptor
options.C: Beta receptor
options.D: Gamma receptor

explanation: The mu receptor is the main target for opioids to kill pain, though it's also why strong opioids can cause drowsiness and slow breathing.

question: A patient on warfarin for a heart condition starts taking a daily garlic supplement. What is the major concern here?

options.A: The combination can significantly increase the risk of bleeding
options.B: The warfarin will turn the garlic tablets into poison
options.C: The patient will develop severe vitamin C toxicity
options.D: The garlic will completely cure the heart condition overnight

explanation: Garlic naturally thins the blood a little. Combined with warfarin, it can dangerously boost the bleeding risk. Always screen for herbal-drug interactions!

question: Why is 'modifiability' an important factor when deciding which health problem to tackle first?

options.A: It proves that chronic diseases are always easier to cure than acute infections
options.B: It eliminates the need for community participation in health planning
options.C: It guarantees that the local government will increase taxes for health programs
options.D: It ensures the team focuses on problems that can realistically be solved with available resources

explanation: Modifiability looks at whether an intervention can actually make a difference given current technology, funding, and staff capacity. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T4#GNS124_U3_T4_h8)

question: Why do community nurses still use paper records and stationery instead of computers all the time?

options.A: Community outposts often lack reliable computer networks and digital infrastructure
options.B: Paper forms are legally required to be more accurate than digital files
options.C: Rural patients refuse to let nurses use computers near them
options.D: Computers cannot store health data related to immunization

explanation: Spot on! Because remote health posts and home visits rarely have steady electricity or internet, good old paper remains our most practical tool.

question: Which medication class is most commonly used to reduce severe inflammation inside an arthritic joint?

options.A: Inhaled bronchodilators
options.B: Topical antifungal creams
options.C: Oral loop diuretics
options.D: Corticosteroids

explanation: Corticosteroids are powerful anti-inflammatory drugs frequently injected into joints to calm swelling and pain. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T9#GNS125_U3_T9_h4)

question: How does endocrine hyposecretion usually show up in a patient over time?

options.A: It usually develops slowly over a long period
options.B: It appears suddenly within a few hours
options.C: It fluctuates wildly every single day
options.D: It only occurs after a major surgical operation

explanation: Most of the time, glands get tired or damaged gradually, so symptoms creep up slowly rather than hitting all at once.

question: What is the main purpose of nursing research informatics?

options.A: Managing daily staff shift rosters and nurse-to-patient ratios
options.B: Supporting data collection and analysis to discover new nursing knowledge
options.C: Ordering routine hospital supplies and medical equipment inventory
options.D: Providing health tips and reminders to patients via mobile phones

explanation: Research informatics uses technology to manage studies, analyze data, and build the evidence base for nursing practice. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T2#GNS113_U1_T2_h5)

question: You notice a fellow nurse showing signs of severe impairment while on duty. What is the best professional step to take?

options.A: Keep the secret permanently and let the impaired nurse handle critical drug doses alone
options.B: Report the observation safely through institutional channels to protect patients and help the colleague
options.C: Steal some of the leftover medications for personal use after the shift ends
options.D: Shout insults at the colleague in front of patients and visitors in the hallway

explanation: Patient safety always comes first, but we also want to guide our struggling colleagues toward the help they need through proper, confidential channels.

question: Why is consistency in data collection so important during the empirical phase?

options.A: It guarantees that every participant will receive financial payment
options.B: It allows researchers to finish their shifts earlier in the day
options.C: It stops patients from asking questions about their treatment
options.D: It prevents errors and ensures measurements are reliable across all participants

explanation: If data is gathered differently for each person, the final results will be skewed and untrustworthy. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T1#GNS217_U3_T1_h5)

question: What is the primary purpose of using IEC support materials during a health talk?

options.A: To reinforce key health messages and make them easy to remember
options.B: To completely replace the need for verbal health education
options.C: To decorate the community health center walls
options.D: To serve as official medical prescriptions for patients

explanation: Support materials provide visual and tactile reminders that help people retain health information long after the meeting ends. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T4#GNS124_U5_T4_h2)

question: A mother denies her toddler eggs due to a local belief. What is the biggest danger of this practice?

options.A: Immediate development of a severe infectious disease
options.B: Complete immunity to childhood vitamin deficiencies
options.C: Deprivation of high-quality animal protein essential for growth
options.D: Rapid improvement in the child's daily speech patterns

explanation: Eggs are tiny powerhouses of protein and nutrients! Keeping them away from growing toddlers robs their bodies of what they need to build strong muscles and brains.

question: How are public health care providers mainly funded?

options.A: Direct patient user fees collected at each visit
options.B: Government tax revenues and public allocations
options.C: International NGO grants and foreign loans exclusively
options.D: Private donations and corporate investments only

explanation: Exactly! Public hospitals and clinics rely heavily on government budgets and taxes to keep their doors open for everyone.

question: What is the very first thing you should do right after giving an injection?

options.A: Break the needle off the syringe barrel before throwing it in the trash
options.B: Activate the safety device and drop the syringe into a sharps container
options.C: Recap the needle firmly using both hands to protect housekeeping staff
options.D: Place the exposed needle on the bedside tray until documentation is done

explanation: Safety first! Never recap needles with two hands. Pop the safety shield on and drop the whole syringe straight into the sharps box to avoid nasty needle-stick injuries.

question: Which of the following statements about legally blind individuals is true?

options.A: Most retain some form of residual vision or light perception
options.B: They cannot hear or speak normally compared to others
options.C: They experience total pitch darkness without any exceptions
options.D: Their condition can always be cured with minor surgery

explanation: Legal blindness is a definition for benefits and care, but very few people with this status see absolute blackness; most have usable light or shape awareness. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T8#GNS324_U4_T8_h3)

question: Why is the home health nurse often described as the central communication hub?

options.A: They make all final medical diagnoses without consulting a physician
options.B: They are the only healthcare worker allowed to visit the residence
options.C: They manage the central telephone switchboard for the health agency
options.D: They connect the patient, family, doctors, and therapists together

explanation: Because nurses visit frequently, they coordinate information between all the different disciplines involved in the patient's care. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T7#GNS324_U1_T7_h6)

question: During which step of the planning process does a nurse manager weigh the pros and cons of different staffing methods?

options.A: Premising the future
options.B: Establishing the budget
options.C: Setting objectives
options.D: Evaluating alternatives

explanation: Evaluating alternatives involves comparing the advantages and disadvantages of each proposed option before making a final choice. [learn more](GST321_U1_T5#GST321_U1_T5_h4)

question: What fields are combined in nursing informatics?

options.A: Pharmacology, anatomy, and clinical psychology
options.B: Public health, epidemiology, and health economics
options.C: Nursing science, computer science, and information science
options.D: Biology, chemistry, and hospital administration

explanation: Nursing informatics merges nursing principles with computer and information technology to improve data management and patient care outcomes. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T8#GNS113_U1_T8_h1)

question: Why is changing or back-dating a patient's chart after a bad incident a serious offense?

options.A: It violates public health disease reporting laws
options.B: It automatically increases the patient's hospital billing charges
options.C: It destroys the legal integrity and truthfulness of the clinical record
options.D: It prevents the electronic health record from backing up data

explanation: The medical record must always show the true, honest timeline of care. Altering it later destroys trust and patient safety.

question: An investigation team sets a strict standard for what symptoms and lab results a patient must have to be counted in an outbreak. What is this standard called?

options.A: A treatment protocol
options.B: An epidemiological limit
options.C: A surveillance barrier
options.D: A case definition

explanation: A case definition sets clear criteria (clinical signs, time, place) so all investigators count the exact same type of cases. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h5)

question: What kind of survey question gives people a fixed list of choices to pick from?

options.A: Unstructured item
options.B: Open-ended item
options.C: Closed-ended item
options.D: Narrative item

explanation: Closed-ended items restrict answers to predefined options, which makes counting and analyzing the responses much easier for your research project.

question: Which of the following is NOT a way to prepare for or prevent a disaster?

options.A: Ignoring safety regulations in industrial factories to save money
options.B: Stockpiling emergency medical supplies and personal protective gear
options.C: Conducting routine workplace evacuation drills with employees
options.D: Establishing strong communication links between local emergency agencies

explanation: Easy choice! Disregarding safety codes invites disaster rather than preparing for it.

question: Which health indicator typically gets better as a country's GNP goes up?

options.A: Incidence of waterborne diseases
options.B: Infant mortality rate
options.C: General population morbidity
options.D: Rate of chronic malnutrition

explanation: As a nation grows wealthier, it can afford better maternal and child healthcare, which means fewer babies dying in infancy. Great health systems start with strong economies!

question: A new mother looks exhausted and tells you she feels totally hopeless weeks after delivery. What should you do first?

options.A: Provide a supportive listening ear and involve family in her care
options.B: Tell her to ignore her feelings and focus entirely on chores
options.C: Leave her alone so she can sleep without any interruptions
options.D: Advise her to stop breastfeeding immediately to gain rest

explanation: Start by listening without judgment and bringing her support system on board. Validating her feelings is a great first step toward healing.

question: What is the correct order for putting on (donning) your PPE before entering an isolation room?

options.A: Mask first, then gloves, gown, and eye protection
options.B: Gloves first, then gown, mask, and protective eyewear
options.C: Eye protection first, followed by gloves, gown, and mask
options.D: Gown first, then mask or respirator, eye protection, and gloves

explanation: Great job! You start by covering your body with the gown, secure your breathing and eyes, and pull your glove cuffs over the gown sleeves last so there are no skin gaps.

question: Which of these is NOT something a nurse checks for safety during a first home visit?

options.A: Safety and cleanliness of the water supply
options.B: Presence of loose rugs or cluttered walkways
options.C: Condition of electrical wiring and cooking areas
options.D: Availability of high-tech robotic surgery equipment

explanation: Correct! We don't expect high-tech operating theatre equipment in a house. Our focus is purely on everyday home safety hazards.

question: Out of the common types of vaginitis, which one is officially classified as a sexually transmitted infection (STI)?

options.A: Atrophic vaginitis
options.B: Trichomoniasis
options.C: Vulvovaginal candidiasis
options.D: Bacterial vaginosis

explanation: Trichomoniasis is caused by a tiny parasite and is primarily passed along through sexual contact. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T10#GNS216_U5_T10_h2)

question: Which of these is the best example of a hospital-wide policy that applies to everyone?

options.A: Triage categorization rules inside the emergency room
options.B: General fire evacuation and safety rules for all staff
options.C: The exact step-by-step scrub technique for the surgical theater
options.D: Pediatric drug dosage calculation tables for infants

explanation: Fire safety and basic institutional conduct apply to every single worker in the building, making them hospital-wide policies.

question: A client complains that taking a daily pill is too hard with her busy work schedule. What is a great recommendation to discuss?

options.A: Double the daily pill dose to make up for missed days
options.B: Scold the client for being irresponsible with her medication
options.C: Stop using all forms of contraception immediately
options.D: Discuss long-acting reversible options like implants or injectables

explanation: If daily pills are a struggle, methods like injectables or implants take away the stress of daily remembering while offering great protection.

question: During a home visit at 34 weeks, you notice the home has no clean running water or good lighting. What is your best move?

options.A: Ignore the issue since delivery is still weeks ahead
options.B: Help the family plan how to store clean water and arrange good lighting for the birth
options.C: Advise the mother to move to a relative's house in another town
options.D: Cancel the home birth plan immediately without discussing alternatives

explanation: As a supportive nurse, you help problem-solve practical needs with the family ahead of time so they are fully ready for the big day.

question: When should a nurse use soap and water instead of an alcohol hand rub?

options.A: When the clinic runs out of clean disposable gloves
options.B: Only at the very beginning of the morning shift
options.C: Before opening every single new vaccine vial
options.D: When hands are visibly soiled with dirt or body fluids

explanation: Soap and water are required to physically wash away visible dirt, grime, and certain types of spores that alcohol rubs cannot clear effectively. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T67#GNS214_U1_T67_h2)

question: What is a major financial headache caused by unreliable public electricity in Nigerian hospitals?

options.A: Automatic shutdown of all nursing schools
options.B: Heavy financial expenditure on diesel generators
options.C: Immediate reduction in patient admission rates
options.D: Instant conversion of hospitals to digital clinics

explanation: Spot on! Hospitals have to spend a massive chunk of their budgets buying diesel just to keep emergency lights and life-saving machines running.

question: What is a major logistical problem caused by uncoordinated disaster donations?

options.A: Relief workers spend all their time cooking donated food
options.B: Local markets experience a permanent surplus of luxury vehicles
options.C: Hospitals run out of storage space for monetary funds
options.D: Unwanted goods block transport routes while essential items get stuck

explanation: Sending random unrequested supplies clogs up ports and roads, delaying the delivery of life-saving medical gear. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T7#GNS315_U5_T7_h6)

question: What is the main goal of doing a root cause analysis after a safety incident happens?

options.A: To increase the paperwork burden for the nursing shift supervisor
options.B: To hide the mistake from hospital management and legal authorities
options.C: To uncover underlying system failures and prevent future occurrences
options.D: To find the specific nurse to blame and recommend immediate termination

explanation: Root cause analysis isn't about finger-pointing; it's about fixing broken systems so the same mistake never happens again.

question: Which type of teeth are primarily designed for biting and cutting food?

options.A: Incisors
options.B: Canines
options.C: Premolars
options.D: Molars

explanation: Incisors are the sharp, flat front teeth used specifically for biting off pieces of food. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T1#GNS121_U1_T1_h4)

question: Why do unsafe injections carry a higher risk than many other medical exposures?

options.A: They always involve contaminated intravenous fluids
options.B: They cause immediate systemic allergic reactions
options.C: They are usually performed by untrained family members
options.D: They introduce pathogens directly past the body's skin barrier

explanation: Normally, our skin and mucous membranes act as strong shields against germs. An injection skips past that natural barrier, sending germs straight into tissue or blood. Brilliant logic to keep in mind!

question: If an abscess cavity has been packed with gauze, when is the patient usually asked to return for a check-up?

options.A: In one month for suture removal
options.B: Only if severe pain returns
options.C: After exactly two full weeks
options.D: Within 24 to 48 hours

explanation: Patients with packed wounds need a quick follow-up in 1 to 2 days so the healthcare team can check the healing and start removing the packing material.

question: What makes a competitive antagonist unique?

options.A: It destroys the agonist molecules inside the bloodstream
options.B: It binds to a completely different site on the cell
options.C: It fights with the agonist for the same receptor site
options.D: It changes the chemical structure of the target organ

explanation: Competitive means they are wrestling for the exact same parking spot (receptor site)! Whoever gets there first or has more numbers wins the spot.

question: Where are surgical family planning procedures, like tubal ligation, usually performed?

options.A: Secondary or tertiary hospital
options.B: Mobile immunization outreach post
options.C: Primary health post
options.D: Community pharmacy shop

explanation: Major surgeries need sterile operating theatres and specialized surgical teams found in our bigger hospitals.

question: Which piece of equipment do you need to safely connect an oxygen mask to a hospital wall supply?

options.A: Sphygmomanometer
options.B: Suction canister
options.C: Flowmeter
options.D: Glucometer strip

explanation: The flowmeter plugs into the wall outlet so you can easily control and measure the liters per minute flowing to the patient.

question: Which of these is NOT a common reason why nurses resist workplace change?

options.A: Cynicism caused by past failed projects
options.B: Fear of appearing incompetent with new technology
options.C: Desire to increase overall patient hospital stays
options.D: Fatigue from working understaffed shifts

explanation: You got this! Nurses resist due to fear, fatigue, or routine disruption, but nobody wants patients staying in the hospital longer than needed.

question: Which enzyme makes cyclic GMP (cGMP) inside smooth muscle cells?

options.A: Nitric oxide synthase
options.B: Phosphodiesterase type 5
options.C: Acetylcholinesterase
options.D: Guanylyl cyclase

explanation: You nailed it! Nitric oxide activates guanylyl cyclase, which builds cGMP to help relax the muscles.

question: What is the primary role of instructional materials in nursing education?

options.A: To eliminate the need for textbooks
options.B: To grade student practical examinations
options.C: To replace the clinical instructor entirely
options.D: To make learning and teaching more effective

explanation: Instructional materials are designed to support educators in delivering clear lessons and helping students grasp complex concepts more easily. [learn more](GST321_U8_T4#GST321_U8_T4_h1)

question: Why is it strongly preferred to give vasopressors through a central line rather than a peripheral vein?

options.A: Leaking into surrounding tissues can cause severe tissue damage and necrosis
options.B: Central lines deliver medication directly to the kidneys faster
options.C: Vasopressors dissolve peripheral plastic catheters very quickly
options.D: Peripheral veins are completely unable to absorb liquid medications

explanation: Vasopressors cause such intense blood vessel constriction that any leakage outside a peripheral vein cuts off local blood supply and destroys tissue. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T5#GNS123_U3_T5_h7)

question: Why might a misguided healthcare worker agree to perform FGM?

options.A: They are legally required to obey local cultural traditions
options.B: They want to prevent the girl from going to a traditional cutter
options.C: Standard nursing school curricula train them for the procedure
options.D: Hospital management mandates the procedure to generate revenue

explanation: Some clinicians wrongly think they are 'harm reductionists' by doing a 'cleaner cut' than traditional practitioners, but performing FGM is never okay.

question: What does syndromic surveillance primarily track during a health emergency?

options.A: Only confirmed laboratory cases of rare tropical diseases
options.B: Hospital staff attendance records during a night shift
options.C: Groups of symptoms before laboratory tests are confirmed
options.D: The exact financial cost of medical equipment used

explanation: Syndromic surveillance watches symptom patterns early on, allowing teams to act fast without waiting for slow lab test results. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T2#GNS315_U5_T2_h4)

question: What is the primary goal of remote patient monitoring tools?

options.A: To track patient health metrics from a distance and alert nurses to dangerous changes
options.B: To broadcast educational health videos on community television channels
options.C: To monitor hospital inventory levels and surgical equipment supplies
options.D: To replace all in-person physical therapy sessions for recovering patients

explanation: Correct! Remote tools let patients check vital signs at home so nurses can spot warning signs early, even from miles away.

question: When can a nurse researcher safely reject the null hypothesis?

options.A: When the calculated p-value is less than or equal to alpha
options.B: When the nursing supervisor demands positive outcomes from the ward
options.C: When the sample size consists of more than ten patients
options.D: When the p-value is much higher than the chosen significance level

explanation: Spot on. When your p-value drops below your set alpha (like 0.05), you have strong enough evidence to say your intervention truly worked!

question: A patient comes to the surgical ward with a suspected knee injury involving a torn ligament. Which diagnostic test is the nurse most likely to prepare the patient for?

options.A: Routine urinalysis
options.B: Electrocardiogram
options.C: Standard chest X-ray
options.D: Magnetic Resonance Imaging

explanation: Ligaments are soft tissues inside a joint, making MRI the ideal test to check for tears. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T12#GNS123_U2_T12_h3)

question: Why might a patient hide important health details during a clinic visit?

options.A: A preference for written instructions over verbal communication
options.B: Fear of judgment due to rigid gender assumptions
options.C: The absence of institutional billing systems
options.D: Lack of basic understanding of biological sex

explanation: You got it! If patients feel we hold stereotypes, they worry about being judged and will keep quiet about sensitive issues.

question: Why do we apply heavy oil or petroleum jelly over a skin boil that has a fly larva inside?

options.A: To dissolve the outer skin layer and make surgical cutting unnecessary
options.B: To cool down the local inflammation and numb the severe pain instantly
options.C: To block the breathing hole and force the larva to crawl out for air
options.D: To poison the parasite with chemical toxins absorbed through its skin

explanation: Smothering the breathing hole cuts off their oxygen supply, tricking the larva into crawling out where you can safely remove it. Clever nursing trick!

question: What are the normal blood vessels found inside a healthy newborn umbilical cord?

options.A: Two arteries and one vein
options.B: Three arteries and two veins
options.C: Two veins and one artery
options.D: One artery and one vein

explanation: Think 'AVA': Artery, Vein, Artery (two arteries, one vein). Finding this normal trio is a great reassuring sign during assessment!

question: A patient with type 2 diabetes asks why they need to eat more fiber. How should you explain it?

options.A: Fiber slows down digestion, which helps prevent sharp blood sugar spikes after meals
options.B: Fiber increases blood sugar levels rapidly for quick energy
options.C: Fiber completely cures diabetes within a few days of eating it
options.D: Fiber replaces the need to ever take diabetes medication again

explanation: Great nursing communication! Fiber slows down how fast sugar enters the blood, keeping those glucose levels nice and steady after eating.

question: What does 'data saturation' mean during qualitative interviews?

options.A: All participants have completed their medical treatments
options.B: The researcher has run out of financial funding for the study
options.C: The audio recording devices have stopped working properly
options.D: No new information or themes are emerging from interviews

explanation: Think of a sponge that is fully soaked. Saturation means you've heard it all; conducting more interviews isn't bringing up anything new, so you can wrap up!

question: A client expresses fear that an injectable contraceptive will cause permanent infertility. What is the best nursing response?

options.A: Agree that hormonal drugs permanently damage the womb and suggest avoiding them
options.B: Insist she takes the injection anyway because healthcare workers know best
options.C: Explain that fertility generally returns after the drug wears off, though it may take a few months
options.D: Tell the client that her fears are unfounded and scold her for listening to myths

explanation: Nurses must address client fears respectfully with accurate medical facts rather than dismissing or forcing them. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T7#GNS216_U1_T7_h3)

question: Why is getting a high percentage of a community vaccinated so important?

options.A: It establishes herd immunity to reduce the spread of disease
options.B: It guarantees that innate barriers never fail under stress
options.C: It prevents allergies from developing in newborn infants
options.D: It permanently eliminates all environmental germs from the earth

explanation: Herd immunity creates a protective ring around vulnerable people who can't get vaccinated, slowing down or stopping the spread of disease.

question: Which organization sets the rules and scope of practice for nurses right here in Nigeria?

options.A: World Health Organization Africa
options.B: Nigerian Medical Association
options.C: Federal Ministry of Information
options.D: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria

explanation: That's the NMCN! They guide our training, exams, and professional practice across Nigeria.

question: What is a transitional enclave model in sheltered employment?

options.A: A small group working inside a regular business with a job coach
options.B: A workshop that only operates during the night shift
options.C: A factory run entirely by robotic machines without humans
options.D: An online virtual office where clients work from home

explanation: An enclave places clients right inside a normal workplace while giving them the safety net of special supervision. You're crushing your studies!

question: How does opening up the space between spinal bones help a patient with a pinched nerve?

options.A: It permanently fuses the spinal bones together
options.B: It stops blood flow to the nerve root
options.C: It stretches the spinal cord until it snaps
options.D: It reduces pressure on the compressed nerve

explanation: Think of it like giving the nerve some breathing room! When the bones are pulled slightly apart, the squeeze is lifted, easing pain and numbness.

question: How does hyperemesis gravidarum differ from normal pregnancy morning sickness?

options.A: It only occurs during the final trimester of pregnancy
options.B: It causes severe, unstoppable vomiting leading to dehydration and weight loss
options.C: It has no effect on the overall fluid balance of the body
options.D: It usually resolves completely within the first four weeks

explanation: While normal morning sickness is manageable, hyperemesis involves nonstop vomiting that drains the body's fluids and nutrition. Great job keeping the clinical differences clear!

question: Why are hip and spine fractures very common in elderly patients with weakened bones?

options.A: These bones are made entirely of cartilage instead of bone.
options.B: These regions contain high amounts of fragile cancellous bone.
options.C: These bones are never protected by muscle tissue.
options.D: These areas never undergo normal bone remodeling.

explanation: Areas like the hip, wrist, and spine are packed with delicate cancellous (spongy) bone. When someone develops osteoporosis, these spongy areas lose their strength first, making them prime spots for fractures.

question: What does the term 'attrition' mean in longitudinal research?

options.A: The gradual wearing out of medical testing equipment
options.B: The process of cleaning data in a computer spreadsheet
options.C: A sudden increase in hospital funding for research
options.D: Participants dropping out or leaving the study over time

explanation: You nailed it! Attrition simply means losing participants along the way due to factors like moving away or getting tired of the study.

question: Which of these actions does NOT support safe patient care by a nurse leader?

options.A: Maintaining adequate staffing levels for patient acuity
options.B: Ensuring evidence-based clinical guidelines are followed
options.C: Punishing staff publicly for reporting near-misses
options.D: Promoting open communication and incident reporting

explanation: Spot on! Publicly punishing staff for speaking up only creates fear, making people hide their mistakes and putting patients at greater risk.

question: How should a nurse protect a patient's dignity during a bedside handover?

options.A: Speak in a very loud voice so everyone in the hallway can hear
options.B: Ask all family members to permanently leave the hospital ward
options.C: Ensure privacy curtains are drawn and sensitive details are discussed discreetly
options.D: Refuse to let the patient look at their own medical chart

explanation: Always draw privacy curtains and keep your voice soft and respectful when talking about private health matters.

question: Why do hospitals team up with legal aid groups and local shelters when caring for survivors?

options.A: To reduce the number of follow-up clinic visits required
options.B: To provide comprehensive support that addresses safety, housing, and justice
options.C: To transfer all medical responsibilities away from the nursing staff
options.D: To ensure that the hospital makes a profit from court fees

explanation: You got it! Healing takes more than medicine—teamwork helps survivors find safety, shelter, and justice all in one go.

question: Which of the following is a core objective of government food intervention?

options.A: Ensuring food security for all citizens
options.B: Eliminating all small-scale family farming
options.C: Maximizing profits for fast-food corporations
options.D: Guaranteeing free food for international export

explanation: Food security is a primary objective, ensuring that everyone has access to safe and nutritious food. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T028#GNS227_U2_T028_h2)

question: At what time of day is a blood test most accurate for checking testosterone levels?

options.A: Right before bedtime
options.B: Late afternoon
options.C: Immediately after a heavy meal
options.D: Early morning

explanation: Testosterone levels naturally peak in the early morning hours, so doctors prefer drawing blood then for the most reliable results.

question: Which of these is a key part of psychological first aid provided by nurses after a disaster?

options.A: Prescribing heavy antipsychotic medication to all victims
options.B: Diagnosing long-term psychiatric disorders on the spot
options.C: Forcing survivors to recount traumatic details immediately
options.D: Offering a calm presence and practical assistance

explanation: You got it! Psychological first aid is all about being a calming, safe support and helping with basic needs—never forcing people to talk about trauma.

question: An adult female patient refuses a procedure, but her husband insists you must do it anyway. What should you do?

options.A: Discharge the patient immediately without explanation
options.B: Obey the husband because he is the head of the household
options.C: Respect the patient's autonomous refusal and maintain her confidentiality
options.D: Perform the procedure secretly without the patient knowing

explanation: Every competent adult has the final say over her own body. A patient's right to refuse always overrides outside family demands. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h4)

question: What does an AED do if it detects asystole (a flat line) during its rhythm check?

options.A: It advises against a shock and instructs CPR
options.B: It waits for a medical doctor to override the device
options.C: It switches automatically to an internal pacemaker mode
options.D: It delivers a high-voltage shock immediately

explanation: A flat line (asystole) means there's no electrical activity to shock back into place. The machine knows this, so it will tell you 'no shock advised' and prompt you to keep doing CPR.

question: What is the main job of albumin, an important protein found in our blood?

options.A: Maintaining fluid balance inside blood vessels
options.B: Carrying oxygen directly to the brain cells
options.C: Fighting off acute bacterial infections
options.D: Providing quick energy during intense exercise

explanation: Think of albumin like a tiny sponge inside your blood vessels. It holds onto water so fluid doesn't leak out into the tissues and cause swelling (edema).

question: Which complication is a top cause of mothers dying during home deliveries?

options.A: Post-term pregnancy
options.B: Mild urinary frequency
options.C: Gestational diabetes
options.D: Postpartum hemorrhage

explanation: Heavy bleeding after birth happens fast and can be very dangerous—it's the leading killer of mothers in home birth settings.

question: Why is propylthiouracil (PTU) preferred over methimazole during early pregnancy?

options.A: Methimazole is linked to specific birth defects during early pregnancy
options.B: PTU crosses the human placenta much faster than methimazole
options.C: PTU stays active in pregnant women for up to one full week
options.D: Methimazole stimulates uterine contractions and causes early labor

explanation: We avoid methimazole in the first trimester because it carries a risk of birth defects, making PTU the safer choice for mum and baby.

question: Which insect is the main carrier that spreads yellow fever in towns and cities?

options.A: Tsetse fly
options.B: Aedes aegypti mosquito
options.C: House fly
options.D: Anopheles mosquito

explanation: Great job! The Aedes aegypti mosquito lives close to human homes, making it the primary villain in spreading urban yellow fever. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T9#GNS214_U1_T9_h2)

question: What is the main focus of a maternity home in the community?

options.A: Managing low-risk pregnancies and normal deliveries
options.B: Treating chronic illnesses in elderly patients
options.C: Performing major complex obstetric surgeries
options.D: Providing long-term pediatric intensive care

explanation: You've got this! Maternity homes are set up to handle normal, healthy pregnancies and deliveries right in the neighborhood.

question: Immediately after a natural disaster, what is a top health priority for teams like the WHO?

options.A: Issuing passports to displaced citizens
options.B: Managing international commercial trade agreements
options.C: Designing long-term economic policies for the affected country
options.D: Preventing secondary health crises like waterborne disease outbreaks

explanation: Well done! When clean water systems break down, diseases like cholera can spread fast, so stopping secondary outbreaks is a top priority.

question: On a quality improvement team, what is the data analyst's main job?

options.A: Resolves personal conflicts between staff members
options.B: Leads bedside patient care procedures every shift
options.C: Runs team meetings and keeps the group focused
options.D: Collects and interprets numbers related to the project

explanation: You got it! The data analyst looks at the numbers and metrics to check progress and prove whether a new change is actually making things better.

question: What is the main benefit of involving local community members when planning health programs?

options.A: It guarantees that patients will pay high fees for services
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for professional nurses
options.C: It ensures the programs are culturally acceptable and sustainable
options.D: It allows the federal government to stop funding local health centers

explanation: Correct! When communities help design their own health programs, they take ownership and keep them running successfully for the long haul.

question: What term is used when people delay or refuse vaccines even though they are available?

options.A: Herd immunity
options.B: Vaccine hesitancy
options.C: Cold chain failure
options.D: Antigen fatigue

explanation: Spot on! 'Vaccine hesitancy' describes when people feel unsure or hold back from getting vaccinated due to various doubts or worries.

question: What is the body's main use for carbohydrates?

options.A: Building structural support for internal organs
options.B: Acting as cofactors for enzyme production
options.C: Transporting fat-soluble vitamins through blood
options.D: Providing a quick and primary source of energy

explanation: Spot on! Carbs break down easily into glucose, giving your body and brain the fast fuel needed to power through the day.

question: What is the first phase of the nursing process?

options.A: Diagnosis
options.B: Assessment
options.C: Planning
options.D: Evaluation

explanation: Assessment is always the starting point, where the nurse collects all necessary information about the patient. [learn more](GST319_U4_T2#GST319_U4_T2_h3)

question: Which condition makes the rectal route unsafe because of a high risk of bleeding?

options.A: Mild tension headache
options.B: Simple upper respiratory infection
options.C: Severe thrombocytopenia
options.D: Chronic ankle swelling

explanation: Low platelet counts mean any trauma to the rectal lining can lead to serious, hard-to-stop bleeding. You've got this!

question: What do endocrine glands release straight into the bloodstream?

options.A: Hormones
options.B: Mucus
options.C: Saliva
options.D: Enzymes

explanation: Spot on! Endocrine glands don't use ducts; they release hormones straight into our blood to act as chemical messengers all over the body.

question: Why are elderly individuals at higher risk for severe burn injuries from hot water?

options.A: Their skin is thinner and loses sensitivity
options.B: They prefer much hotter bath temperatures
options.C: Their homes lack modern plumbing systems
options.D: They spend more time cooking than younger adults

explanation: Thinning skin and reduced nerve sensitivity mean older adults may not feel extreme heat quickly enough to pull away. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T4#GNS324_U6_T4_h4)

question: What do we call the continuous, systematic collection of health data for public health action?

options.A: Medical audit
options.B: Randomized sampling
options.C: Clinical trial
options.D: Disease surveillance

explanation: Spot on! Surveillance means keeping a steady watch on disease trends so health workers can act fast. Keep up the momentum!

question: What is the single best way to prevent a catheter-associated urinary tract infection (CAUTI)?

options.A: Clamp the catheter for two hours every afternoon
options.B: Remove the catheter as soon as it is no longer medically necessary
options.C: Apply antibiotic ointment around the meatus three times a day
options.D: Disconnect the drainage tubing every morning to flush it out

explanation: You've got it! The golden rule of preventing catheter infections is taking the tube out the moment it's no longer needed.

question: Intimate partner violence (IPV) often starts quietly. Which behavior is a typical early warning sign?

options.A: Sudden financial ruin orchestrated by external family members
options.B: Unprovoked legal action regarding property ownership
options.C: Immediate and severe physical assaults in public places
options.D: Subtle emotional degradation and controlling behaviors

explanation: Well done! IPV rarely starts with physical blows; it usually creeps in through subtle control, insults, and isolation before turning physical. Always keep your eyes open for these red flags!

question: How does task-shifting help improve healthcare in understaffed rural areas?

options.A: By moving specialist obstetricians to every village clinic in the country
options.B: By transferring pregnant patients to urban centers permanently
options.C: By replacing all nurses with automated computer systems
options.D: By training community health workers to safely deliver certain basic health interventions

explanation: You nailed it! Task-shifting bridges the staff gap by letting trained community workers handle basic, safe tasks when professional nurses aren't enough.

question: How does medication non-compliance affect the wider healthcare system?

options.A: It eliminates waste by saving unused medication supplies
options.B: It increases hospital admissions and strains public health resources
options.C: It lowers the overall cost of running emergency wards
options.D: It reduces the need for expensive pharmaceutical stockpiles

explanation: Spot on. When patients skip doses, preventable complications land them right back in our hospital beds, stretching our resources thin.

question: Which diagnostic test involves placing dye in the rectum to see if it stains a vaginal gauze?

options.A: Cervical smear test
options.B: Barium swallow study
options.C: Methylene blue dye test
options.D: Intravenous pyelogram

explanation: The methylene blue test helps confirm the presence of a tract by tracking fluid movement from the rectum into the vagina. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h5)

question: A patient arrives at the clinic with severe vomiting and dehydration. Why is an IV line started instead of just giving them oral rehydration drinks?

options.A: The patient's digestive tract cannot absorb any liquids safely.
options.B: Oral fluids take too long to reach the stomach lining.
options.C: IV fluids rapidly restore circulating blood volume and correct electrolytes.
options.D: Intravenous fluids taste much better than oral rehydration salts.

explanation: Great thinking! When someone is vomiting heavily, IV fluids are the quickest way to restore circulating blood volume and get their electrolytes balanced safely.

question: What is the most accurate way to measure energy use in a critical care patient?

options.A: Indirect calorimetry
options.B: Skinfold caliper tests
options.C: Standard food diaries
options.D: Body mass index charts

explanation: Indirect calorimetry measures the gases a patient breathes out to figure out their exact calorie needs. It's the gold standard in the ICU!

question: What does true professional accountability mean for a nurse leader?

options.A: Take personal ownership of actions, decisions, and outcomes
options.B: Blame junior staff whenever a clinical mistake happens
options.C: Keep all patient safety data hidden from the public
options.D: Delegate all disciplinary actions to hospital administrators

explanation: Accountability means standing tall and owning your choices—taking credit when things go well, and accepting responsibility when things go wrong.

question: What does standard deviation mainly tell us about a set of healthcare data?

options.A: The frequency of the most common clinical symptom
options.B: How much scores deviate from the mean on average
options.C: The total number of patients who participated in the study
options.D: The exact mathematical difference between the highest and lowest scores

explanation: Think of standard deviation as measuring how spread out the data is. It tells us the average distance that scores fall away from the middle (mean).

question: Why do quality improvement teams prefer small-scale trials over massive, hospital-wide changes?

options.A: Small trials minimize patient risk and allow for quick adjustments
options.B: Hospital management bans large changes of any kind
options.C: Large changes require no documentation or staff meetings
options.D: Small trials are the only way to secure federal research grants

explanation: Starting small is a smart move! It protects patient safety and makes it super easy to tweak things if something isn't working quite right.

question: What is the main purpose of using qualitative tools in a community assessment?

options.A: To capture local attitudes, cultural beliefs, and human stories
options.B: To measure precise blood pressure and body temperature
options.C: To calculate exact mathematical disease prevalence rates
options.D: To count the total number of hospital beds in the district

explanation: Brilliant! Qualitative methods help you understand the 'why' behind people's behaviors rather than just raw numbers.

question: Which of these is NOT a classic warning sign of a growing ovarian tumor?

options.A: Urinary urgency or frequency
options.B: Unexplained weight gain in the upper arms
options.C: Persistent abdominal bloating
options.D: Feeling full very quickly after starting a meal

explanation: Correct! Upper arm weight gain is not linked to ovarian tumors, but bloating, feeling full fast, and rushing to the toilet are classic signs.

question: What is the main goal of contact tracing during an infectious disease outbreak?

options.A: To find out which hospital ward cost the most money
options.B: To collect financial donations from family members
options.C: To monitor exposed individuals and catch new cases early
options.D: To test new pharmaceutical drugs on healthy volunteers

explanation: Well done! Tracking down people who were exposed lets us watch them closely and isolate them before they can spread the illness further.

question: When does bereavement support typically begin and end in a hospice program?

options.A: It begins only after one full year has passed
options.B: It continues for months after the patient passes away
options.C: It only occurs during the final week of the patient's life
options.D: It stops immediately the moment the patient dies

explanation: Bereavement care is an ongoing service that supports grieving family members for many months following their loss. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T14#GNS324_U5_T14_h8)

question: What receptor combination is the trademark of second-generation (atypical) antipsychotics?

options.A: Dopamine and serotonin receptor blockade
options.B: Opioid and adrenergic receptor agonism
options.C: GABA and norepinephrine enhancement
options.D: Histamine and acetylcholine stimulation

explanation: Remember: first-gen mostly blocks dopamine, but second-gen (atypical) agents block both dopamine D2 and serotonin 5-HT2A receptors at the same time.

question: When would you use an independent samples t-test?

options.A: When comparing two completely separate groups of people
options.B: When there is no control group in the study
options.C: When analyzing categorical data with three or more groups
options.D: When measuring the same patients twice over time

explanation: Think 'independent = separate.' Use this when you are comparing two totally different sets of patients, like Ward A versus Ward B.

question: When washing a patient's arms or legs during a bed bath, why does the nurse stroke from the hands or feet toward the torso?

options.A: To check if the patient has broken bones in the hand
options.B: To push all dirt and sweat directly into the armpits
options.C: To make the skin stretch out and look younger
options.D: To promote venous blood return toward the heart

explanation: Brilliant! Moving your washcloth upward helps push venous blood back up toward the heart against gravity, which is great for circulation.

question: Which way of taking misoprostol gets into the bloodstream the fastest?

options.A: Vaginal
options.B: Oral
options.C: Rectal
